desc:
You are given points, an array of integer points [x, y]. Points may repeat. The Manhattan distance between two points is |x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2|.

Return the sum of the Manhattan distances over all pairs i < j, taken modulo 1,000,000,007. Trying every pair directly is too slow for large inputs.

points = [[0,0],[1,2],[3,1]]
pairs: (0,0)-(1,2) = 3,  (0,0)-(3,1) = 4,  (1,2)-(3,1) = 3
result = 10
hints: The absolute difference splits into an x part and a y part, and the two parts can be summed separately.
For one list of numbers, the sum of all pairwise absolute differences becomes easy once the list is sorted. Sort the x values and the y values.
In a sorted list a[0..n-1], the value a[i] is the larger element of i pairs and the smaller element of n - 1 - i pairs. Its net weight is 2i - (n - 1).
editorial: For a fixed pair, |x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2| is the x contribution plus the y contribution. So the total is the sum over all pairs of the x differences, plus the same sum over the y values.

Sort a list of values a. Each value a[i] appears as the larger member of i pairs (with a smaller earlier element), contributing +a[i] each time, and as the smaller member of n - 1 - i pairs, contributing -a[i] each time. Summing gives sum(a[i] * (2i - (n - 1))).
Sorting costs O(n log n) and the rest is linear. Python's integers do not overflow, so the sum can be reduced modulo 1,000,000,007 once at the end.
